title: grothlab/crepas pipeline parameters
description: a reproducible nascent chromatin sequencing analysis pipeline for epigenome replication studies.

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. See [usage docs](https://crepas.grothlab.workers.dev/usage/).

fragment_size.description: Estimated fragment size used to extend single-end reads.

seq_platform.description: Platform/technology used to produce the reads. Corresponds to the `PL` tag in the SAM/BAM file header.
seq_platform.help_text: See the [SAM format specification](https://github.com/samtools/hts-specs/blob/master/SAMv1.pdf). Valid values: CAPILLARY, DNBSEQ (MGI/BGI), ELEMENT, HELICOS, ILLUMINA, IONTORRENT, LS454, ONT (Oxford Nanopore), PACBIO (Pacific Biosciences), SINGULAR, SOLID, and ULTIMA. This field should be omitted when the technology is not in this list (though the PM field may still be present in this case) or is unknown.

seq_center.description: Sequencing center information to be added to read group of BAM files.

read_length.description: Read length used to calculate MACS3 genome size for peak calling if `--macs_gsize` isn't provided.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

reference_genome_options.title: Reference genome options
reference_genome_options.description: Reference genome related files and options required for the workflow.

fasta.description: Path to FASTA genome file. Required unless `--hybrid_fasta` is provided or the file is supplied by a reference genome config (iGenomes/Refgenie).
fasta.help_text: If you don't have the appropriate alignment index available this will be generated for you automatically based on this file. Combine with `--save_reference` to save alignment index for future runs.

spikein_fasta.description: Path to exogenous (spike-in) FASTA genome file. If you provide this, the a hybrid fasta reference file will be generated and used for alignment index building.

hybrid_fasta.description: Path to a pre-built hybrid (endogenous + spike-in) FASTA genome file, with spike-in contigs named `<chromosome_name>_<spikein_genome>`. If provided, this is used directly instead of generating a hybrid fasta from `--fasta`/`--spikein_fasta`. Mutually exclusive with `--fasta`: providing both raises an error.

bwa_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built BWA index.

bwamem2_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built BWAMEM2 index.

minibwa_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built minibwa index.

bowtie_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built Bowtie index.

bowtie2_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built Bowtie2 index.

chromap_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built Chromap index.

star_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built STAR index.

hisat2_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built HISAT2 index.

minimap2_index.description: Path to directory or tar.gz archive for pre-built Minimap2 index.

strobealign_index.description: Path to Strobealign index file with extension '.sti'. This will be created from the FASTA file if not specified and the aligner is set to strobealign.

gene_bed.description: Path to BED file containing gene intervals. This will be created from the GTF file if not specified.

initiation_zones.description: Path to BED file containing initiation zones for SCAR-seq analysis.

okseq_rfd_file.description: Path to GZIP-compressed OK-seq RFD text file. The path cannot contain spaces and must have extension '.txt.gz', '.tsv.gz' or '.bed.gz'

macs_gsize.description: Effective genome size parameter required by MACS3.
macs_gsize.help_text: [Effective genome size](https://github.com/taoliu/MACS#-g--gsize) parameter required by MACS3. Provide the number written out in full (e.g. `--macs_gsize 2700000000`), not in scientific notation: `2.7e9`.

blacklist.description: Path to blacklist regions in BED format, used for filtering alignments.
blacklist.help_text: If provided, alignments that overlap with the regions in this file will be filtered out (see [ENCODE blacklists](https://sites.google.com/site/anshulkundaje/projects/blacklists)). The file should be in BED format.

sparsebed.description: Path to BED file with sparse segments for Consenrich.
sparsebed.help_text: Defines the annotation file of 'sparse segments' (genomic regions) from the complement of an 'inflated' BED file of known active regions. See https://github.com/nolan-h-hamilton/Consenrich/blob/5e7f287d81ac4a9bc098ae29e825a5ded07af3b8/consenrich/consenrich.py#L58C54-L58C174

active_regions.description: Path to BED file with active regions for Consenrich.
active_regions.help_text: Defines the annotation file of 'active regions' (genomic regions) for Consenrich. See https://github.com/nolan-h-hamilton/Consenrich/blob/5e7f287d81ac4a9bc098ae29e825a5ded07af3b8/consenrich/consenrich.py#L67

rocco_params.help_text: CSV file containing chromosome-specific optimization parameters. Each supported genome has a custom `--params` file packaged with ROCCO, but a custom file has to be manually passed to ROCCO within this pipeline. Consider using this argument to set chromosome-specific budget and gamma values custom to your data and preferences. See the [ROCCO documentation](https://nolan-h-hamilton.github.io/ROCCO/#rocco-constants) for more details.

splicesites.description: Path to splice sites file for HISAT2.
splicesites.help_text: If using HISAT2 as the aligner, you can provide a list of known splice sites, which HISAT2 makes use of to align reads with small anchors. If this file is not provided, it will be generated from the GTF file.

save_reference.description: If generated by the pipeline save the BWA index in the results directory.
save_reference.help_text: If the BWA index is generated by the pipeline use this parameter to save it to your results folder. These can then be used for future pipeline runs, reducing processing times.

skip_gtf_index.description: Skip indexing the GTF file with tabix before processing.
skip_gtf_index.help_text: Set this parameter to true to skip indexing the GTF file with tabix. This may be useful if your GTF file is already indexed or if you encounter issues with tabix.

igenomes_base.description: Directory / URL base for iGenomes references.

igenomes_ignore.description: Do not load the iGenomes reference config.
igenomes_ignore.help_text: Do not load `igenomes.config` when running the pipeline. You may choose this option if you observe clashes between custom parameters and those supplied in `igenomes.config`.

refgenie_ignore.description: Whether to ignore the Refgenie reference genomes.
refgenie_ignore.help_text: Do not use the Refgenie reference genomes, even if loaded before through config files.

umi_extraction_and_deduplication_options.title: UMI extraction and deduplication options
umi_extraction_and_deduplication_options.description: Options to adjust UMI extraction and deduplication criteria.

skip_markduplicates.description: Skip the MarkDuplicates step with Picard for samples without UMIs.

umitools_extract_method.help_text: More details can be found in the [UMI-tools documentation](https://umi-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/extract.html#extract-method).

umitools_bc_pattern.help_text: More details can be found in the [UMI-tools documentation](https://umi-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/extract.html#extract-method).
umitools_bc_pattern.description: The UMI barcode pattern to use e.g. 'NNNNNN' indicates that the first 6 nucleotides of the read are from the UMI.

umitools_bc_pattern2.description: The UMI barcode pattern to use if the UMI is located in read 2.

umi_separator.description: Separator used to separate the UMI from the read name.

umi_grouping_method.description: Method to use to determine read groups by subsuming those with similar UMIs. All methods start by identifying the reads with the same mapping position, but treat similar yet nonidentical UMIs differently.

umi_discard_read.description: After UMI barcode extraction discard either R1 or R2 by setting this parameter to `1` or `2`, respectively.

save_dedup_intermeds.description: Save intermediate files from the UMI deduplication step.

skip_split_by_chrom.description: Skip splitting the BAM file by chromosome for UMI deduplication.
skip_split_by_chrom.help_text: BAMs are splitted by chromosome, deduplicated, and then merged back to improve parallelization of the deduplication step. Set this parameter to true to skip this splitting step. This may be useful if you encounter issues with the splitting or merging steps or if your BAM files are small and you don't think that parallelization will speed up the deduplication step.

adapter_trimming_options.title: Adapter trimming options
adapter_trimming_options.description: Options to adjust adapter trimming criteria.

clip_r1.description: Instructs Trim Galore to remove bp from the 5' end of read 1 (or single-end reads).

clip_r2.description: Instructs Trim Galore to remove bp from the 5' end of read 2 (paired-end reads only).

three_prime_clip_r1.description: Instructs Trim Galore to remove bp from the 3' end of read 1 AFTER adapter/quality trimming has been performed.

three_prime_clip_r2.description: Instructs Trim Galore to remove bp from the 3' end of read 2 AFTER adapter/quality trimming has been performed.

trim_full_length.description: Instructs Trim Galore to search for the full length (33 bp) TruSeq (ChIP-seq, ChOR-seq, SCAR-seq) or Nextera (ATAC-seq) adapter sequences for both complement and reverse complements.
trim_full_length.help_text: The default (false) setting will mean that the auto-detect function of Trim Galore will be used. See [https://github.com/FelixKrueger/TrimGalore/blob/master/Docs/Trim_Galore_User_Guide.md#adapter-auto-detection](https://github.com/FelixKrueger/TrimGalore/blob/master/Docs/Trim_Galore_User_Guide.md#adapter-auto-detection)

trim_nextseq.description: Instructs Trim Galore to apply the `--nextseq=X` option, to trim based on quality after removing poly-G tails.
trim_nextseq.help_text: This enables the Cutadapt `--nextseq-trim=3'CUTOFF` option via Trim Galore, which will set a quality cutoff (that is normally given with -q instead), but qualities of G bases are ignored. This trimming is in common for the NextSeq- and NovaSeq-platforms, where basecalls without any signal are called as high-quality G bases. Read the [Cutadapt documentation](https://cutadapt.readthedocs.io/en/stable/guide.html#nextseq-trim) for more details.

trim_stringency.description: Instructs Trim Galore to use this stringency (minimum overlap) when searching for adapter sequences.
trim_stringency.help_text: In other words, to reduce the number of falsely trimmed bases, the alignment algorithm in Trim Galore requires that at least this number of bases of the adapter are aligned to the read. This parameter corresponds to the `--stringency` option in Trim Galore and the `--overlap` option in [Cutadapt](https://cutadapt.readthedocs.io/en/stable/guide.html#random-matches).

trim_error_rate.description: Instructs Trim Galore to use this error rate when trimming.

trim_q_cutoff.description: Instructs Trim Galore to use this quality cutoff when trimming.

trim_minimum_length.description: Instructs Trim Galore to discard reads that became shorter than this length after adapter or quality trimming. A value of 0 effectively disables this behaviour.

trim_maximum_length.description: Instructs Trim Galore to discard reads that are longer than this length after adapter or quality trimming.

skip_trimming.help_text: Use this if your input FastQ files have already been trimmed outside of the workflow or if you're very confident that there is no adapter contamination in your data.

save_trimmed.description: Save the trimmed FastQ files in the results directory.
save_trimmed.help_text: By default, trimmed FastQ files will not be saved to the results directory. Specify this flag (or set to true in your config file) to copy these files to the results directory when complete.

min_trimmed_reads.description: Minimum number of reads required after trimming.

hard_trimming_options.title: Hard trimming options
hard_trimming_options.description: Options to adjust hard trimming criteria.

hardtrim5_length.description: Instructs Trim Galore to hard-trim (shorten) reads to this length from their 3' end. This is performed after adapter/quality trimming.

hardtrim3_length.description: Instructs Trim Galore to hard-trim (shorten) reads to this length from their 5' end. This is performed after adapter/quality trimming.

save_hardtrimmed.description: Whether to save the hard-trimmed reads (FASTQs) in the output directory.

alignment_options.title: Alignment options
alignment_options.description: Options to adjust parameters and filtering criteria for read alignments.

aligner.description: Specifies the alignment algorithm to use.

bwa_min_score.description: Don't output BWA MEM alignments with score lower than this parameter.

bwamem2_min_score.description: Don't output BWAMEM2 alignments with score lower than this parameter.

save_align_intermeds.description: Save the intermediate BAM files from the alignment step.
save_align_intermeds.help_text: By default, intermediate BAM files will not be saved. The final BAM files created after the appropriate filtering step are always saved to limit storage usage. Set this parameter to also save other intermediate BAM files.

save_unaligned.description: Where possible, save unaligned reads from either STAR or HISAT2 to the results directory.
save_unaligned.help_text: This may either be in the form of FastQ or BAM files depending on the options available for that particular tool.

align_end_to_end.description: Wheter to perform end-to-end alignment (only relevant for Bowtie2 and STAR). If set to false, local alignment will be performed.

minimap2_preset.description: Preset to use for minimap2 alignment. See the [minimap2 documentation](https://lh3.github.io/minimap2/minimap2.html) for more details.

minimap2_kmer_length.description: K-mer length to use for minimap2 indexing and alignment. See the [minimap2 documentation](https://lh3.github.io/minimap2/minimap2.html) for more details.

minimap2_min_win_size.description: Minimizer window size to use for minimap2 indexing and alignment. See the [minimap2 documentation](https://lh3.github.io/minimap2/minimap2.html) for more details.

minibwa_preset.description: Preset to use for minibwa alignment. See the [minibwa documentation](https://github.com/lh3/minibwa) for more details.

minibwa_min_seed_length.description: Minimum seed length to use for minibwa alignment. See the [minibwa documentation](https://github.com/lh3/minibwa) for more details.

minibwa_bandwidth.description: Bandwidth to use for minibwa alignment. See the [minibwa documentation](https://github.com/lh3/minibwa) for more details.

spikein_options.title: Spike-in options
spikein_options.description: Options to adjust spike-in splitting criteria.

spikein_genome.description: Name of the spike-in genome (if used in the experiment). The spike-in (exogenous) chromosome names in the `--fasta` and `<aligner>_index` files should have the format `<chromosome_name>_<spikein_genome>`, e.g. `chr1_dm6`.

save_spikein_intermeds.description: Save intermediate files during spike-in splitting and filtering of BAMs. These include the split and filtered BAM files before coordinate-sorting.

multimapper_allocation_options.title: Multimapper allocation options
multimapper_allocation_options.description: Options to adjust multimapper allocation criteria.

multimap_allocation_method.description: Method to allocate multimappers. Not setting this parameter means that multimappers will not be allocated (the default).

allo_mixed_cnn.description: When using Allo for multimapper allocation, use the CNN trained on histone ChIP-seq datasets with mixed peaks, otherwise use the default (narrow). See [allo](https://github.com/seqcode/allo?tab=readme-ov-file#options) for more details.

save_allocation_intermeds.description: Save the intermediate BAM files from the multimapper allocation step.

alignment_shifting_options.title: Alignment shifting options
alignment_shifting_options.description: Options to adjust alignment shifting criteria.

save_shifting_intermeds.description: Whether to save the intermediate files from the alignment shifting (only done on ATAC-seq data).

filtering_options.title: Filtering options
filtering_options.description: Options to adjust filtering criteria for BAM files.

skip_flT3.description: Whether to skip the flT3 filtering step (filtering by mapping quality, which also removes multimapping reads in most cases).

skip_flTbl.description: Whether to skip the blacklist filtering step. This serves to skip the removal of blacklisted regions from the BAM files even if a blacklist BED file is provided.

coverage_and_normalization_options.title: Coverage and normalization options
coverage_and_normalization_options.description: Options to adjust coverage and normalization criteria.

skip_srpm.description: Whether to skip the SRPM normalization step. See the [output documentation](https://crepas.grothlab.workers.dev/output/#normalized-bigwig-files) for more details.

skip_cisrpm.description: Whether to skip the CISRPM normalization step. See the [output documentation](https://crepas.grothlab.workers.dev/output/#normalized-bigwig-files) for more details.

coverage_extend_reads.description: This parameter allows the extension of reads to fragment size. If set, each read is extended, without exception.
coverage_extend_reads.help_text: Single-end: Requires a user specified value for the final fragment length. Reads that already exceed this fragment length will not be extended. Paired-end: Reads with mates are always extended to match the fragment size defined by the two read mates. Unmated reads, mate reads that map too far apart (>4x fragment length) or even map to different chromosomes are treated like single-end reads. The input of a fragment length value is optional. If no value is specified, it is estimated from the data (mean of the fragment size of all mate reads). Read the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/bamCoverage.html#read-processing-options) for more details.

coverage_bin_size.description: Size of the bins, in bases, for the output of the coverage calculation.

coverage_skip_nas.description: This parameter determines if non-covered regions (regions without overlapping reads) should be skipped. The default is to treat those regions as having a value of zero. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/bamCoverage.html#read-coverage-normalization-options) for more details.

skip_signal_vs_input.description: Whether to skip the signal vs input comparison step.

signal_vs_input_operation.description: Operation to perform when comparing IP and input coverage. `soi` is basically the same as `ratio`, although it is computed with a special script. For the rest of the operations, see the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/bigwigCompare.html#named-arguments) for more details.

min_signal_for_soi.description: Minimum signal in the IP bin to be included in the signal over input (SOI) calculation. Otherwise, the the score of that bin is set to `NaN`.

min_input_for_soi.description: Minimum input signal in the input bin to be included in the signal over input (SOI) calculation. Otherwise, the the score of that bin is set to `NaN`.

bw_compare_pseudocount.description: A small number to avoid x/0. Only useful together with `--operation log2` or `--operation ratio`. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/bigwigCompare.html#named-arguments) for more details.

bw_compare_skip_zero_over_zero.description: This parameter determines if regions with zero coverage in both the IP and input should be skipped when comparing IP and input coverage. This is determined BEFORE any applicable pseudocount is added. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/bigwigCompare.html#named-arguments) for more details.

use_flT2_as_total_ref.description: Comma-separated list of histone marks for which downsampling or normalization factors should be calculated using the total number of reads before the quality filtering in flT3. The total mapped reads after flT1 will be used if flT2 was not performed (i.e., when there is no spike-in splitting). For marks/antibodies not in this list the total mapped reads after flT3 will be used for normalization factor calculation.

save_coverage_intermeds.description: Whether to save the intermediate files from the coverage calculation step. These include the coverage files in bedGraph format.

min_reads_for_norm.description: Minimum number of total mapped reads required to include a BAM in any normalization. For example, this prevents having an empty exogenous input control BAM when no reads map to the spike-in genome.

skip_bw_average.description: Whether to skip the generation of average bigWig files across replicates for each sample group.

skip_exo_bw.description: Whether to skip the generation of exogenous bigWig files for each sample.

skip_multibigwigsummary.description: Whether to skip the generation of a table with the bin value for all the samples.

skip_plotcorrelation.description: Whether to skip correlation of multibigwigsummary output.

skip_plotpca.description: Whether to skip PCA of multibigwigsummary output.

bam_downsampling_method.description: Method to downsample BAM files. Leave empty to disable downsampling.
bam_downsampling_method.help_text:
The `min_endo_across` method will downsample all IPs and inputs of the same antibody to the minimum number of endogenous reads across all IPs and inputs of the same antibody.
The `min_exo_across` method will downsample all IPs and inputs of the same antibody to the minimum number of exogenous reads across all IPs and inputs of the same antibody.
The `min_endo_by_type` method will downsample all IPs to the minimum number of endogenous reads across all IPs of the same antibody, and all the inputs to the minimum number of endogenous reads across all inputs of the same antibody.
The `min_exo_by_type` method will downsample all IPs to the minimum number of exogenous reads across all IPs of the same antibody, and all the inputs to the minimum number of exogenous reads across all inputs of the same antibody.

downsampling_endo_threshold.description: Threshold of endogenous mapped reads for downsampling. For downsampling methods that search for the minimum endogenous mapped reads across a set of samples, this parameter will determine the lower limit of that minimum. In other words, the minimum mapped endogenous reads should be the minimum number above the `downsampling_endo_threshold`. If there are no totals above this threshold, then the (true) minimum is used.

downsampling_exo_threshold.description: Threshold of exogenous mapped reads for downsampling. For downsampling methods that search for the minimum exogenous mapped reads across a set of samples, this parameter will determine the lower limit of that minimum. In other words, the minimum mapped exogenous reads should be the minimum number above the `downsampling_exogenous_threshold`. If there are no totals above this threshold, then the (true) minimum is used.

bam_downsampling_strategy.description: Strategy to downsample BAM files. See [Picard](https://gatk.broadinstitute.org/hc/en-us/articles/360036431292-DownsampleSam-Picard) for more details.

bam_downsampling_accuracy.description: Accuracy of downsampling BAM files. See [Picard](https://gatk.broadinstitute.org/hc/en-us/articles/360036431292-DownsampleSam-Picard) for more details.

save_downsampling_intermeds.description: Save the intermediate BAM files from the downsampling step.

tecounting_options.title: TE counting options
tecounting_options.description: Options to adjust transposable element (TE) counting criteria.

skip_tecount_gz.description: Skip gzip compression of TEcount output files.

skip_telocal_gz.description: Skip gzip compression of TElocal output files.

te_counting_mode.description: Method to use for TE counting. See [TEcount's documentation](https://github.com/mhammell-laboratory/TEtranscripts?tab=readme-ov-file#usage-1) for more details.

te_counting_gene_gtf.description: Path to a different gene GTF file for counting with TEcount and TElocal. If not provided, the main `--gtf` file will be used to generate a gene index suitable for TEcount or TElocal, unless the respective prebuilt gene index files are provided.

tecount_gene_index.description: Path to the prebuilt gene index file (.ind) for counting with TEcount. If not provided, this file in `--gtf` will be used to generate a gene index suitable for TEcount.

telocal_gene_index.description: Path to the prebuilt gene index file (.ind) for counting with TElocal. If not provided, this file in `--gtf` will be used to generate a gene index suitable for TElocal.

te_gtf.description: Path to the TE GTF file for counting with TEcount or TElocal. If not provided, this file will be used to generate a TE index suitable for TEcount or TElocal.

tecount_te_index.description: Path to the prebuilt TE index file (.ind) for counting with TEcount. If not provided, this file in `--te_gtf` will be used to generate a TE index suitable for TEcount.

telocal_te_index.description: Path to the prebuilt TE index file (.locInd) for local (instance) TE counting with TElocal. If not provided, this file in `--te_gtf` will be used to generate a TE index suitable for TElocal.

peak_calling_options.title: Peak calling options
peak_calling_options.description: Options to adjust peak calling criteria.

skip_peak_calling.description: Skip peak calling altogether, for every peak caller listed in `peak_callers`.

peak_callers.description: Comma-separated list of peak calling algorithms to use.
peak_callers.help_text: One or more of `macs3`, `genrich`, `consenrich`, `epic2`, `mace`, `dpeak`, `dpos`, `dregion`, `dtriple`, `edd`, `denopa`, `seacr`, given as a comma-separated list without spaces, e.g. `--peak_callers macs3,genrich`. Every listed peak caller is run on all applicable samples. Use `--skip_peak_calling` to switch peak calling off entirely. `denopa` is currently not supported: no usable container for it exists yet.

narrow_peak.description: Whether to call narrow peaks with MACS3 and Genrich. Default is to call broad peaks.

peak_cutoff_method.description: Type of statistical cutoff to use for peak calling.

narrow_cutoff.description: Specifies narrow cutoff value (p-value or q-value) for MACS3 and Genrich peak calling.

broad_cutoff.description: Specifies broad cutoff value (p-value or q-value) for MACS3 and Genrich peak calling.

consensus_min_replicates_per_sample.description: Number of biological replicates required from a given condition for a peak to contribute to a consensus peak.
consensus_min_replicates_per_sample.help_text: If you are confident you have good reproducibility amongst your replicates then you can increase the value of this parameter to create a 'reproducible' set of consensus peaks. For example, a value of 2 will mean peaks that have been called in at least 2 replicates will contribute to the consensus set of peaks, and as such peaks that are unique to a given replicate will be discarded. A value of -1 means that a peak must have been called in all replicates to contribute to the consensus set of peaks.

consensus_peaks_max_dist.description: Maximum distance between peaks allowed for peaks to be merged for consensus peak definition. `--consensus_peaks_max_dist 0` means overlapping and/or book-ended features are merged.

macs_extsize.description: Used to extend reads in 5'->3' direction to fix-sized fragments when processing ATAC-seq data, for which MACS3 bypasses building the shifting model (`--nomodel`). See [MACS3 documentation](https://macs3-project.github.io/MACS/docs/callpeak.html) for more details.

macs_slocal.description: Size of the small local region around peak regions to calculate the maximum lambda as local lambda.
macs_slocal.help_text: By default, MACS3 considers 1000 bp for small local region (`--slocal`). You can tweak this according to your project. Remember that if the region is set too small, a sharp spike in the input data may kill a significant peak. See [MACS3 documentation](https://macs3-project.github.io/MACS/docs/callpeak.html) for more details.

macs_llocal.description: Size of the large local region around peak regions to calculate the maximum lambda as local lambda.
macs_llocal.help_text: By default, MACS3 considers 10000 bp for large local region (`--llocal`) which captures the bias from a long-range effect like an open chromatin domain. You can tweak this according to your project. See [MACS3 documentation](https://macs3-project.github.io/MACS/docs/callpeak.html) for more details.

save_macs_pileup.description: Instruct MACS3 to create bedGraph files normalised to signal per million reads.

skip_peak_qc.description: Skip MACS3 peak QC plot generation.

skip_peak_annotation.description: Skip annotation of MACS3 and consensus peaks with HOMER.

skip_consensus_peaks.description: Skip consensus peak generation, annotation and counting.

skip_consensus_plotprofile.description: Skip generation of the consensus peak profile plot.

consensus_plotprofile_mode.description: Mode to use for the consensus peak profile plot. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/plotProfile.html#mode) for more details.

consensus_plotprofile_ref_point.description: Reference point to use for the consensus peak profile plot when `--consensus_plotprofile_mode` is set to `reference_point`. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/plotProfile.html#reference-point) for more details.

consensus_plotprofile_region_body_length.description: Length of the region body to plot for the consensus peak profile plot when `--consensus_plotprofile_mode` is set to `scale_regions`. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/plotProfile.html#scale-regions) for more details.

consensus_plotprofile_upstream.description: Length of the upstream region to plot for the consensus peak profile plot. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/plotProfile.html#upstream-and-downstream) for more details.

consensus_plotprofile_downstream.description: Length of the downstream region to plot for the consensus peak profile plot. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/plotProfile.html#upstream-and-downstream) for more details.

consensus_plotprofile_skip_zeros.description: Whether to skip regions with zero coverage in the consensus peak profile plot. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/plotProfile.html#skip-zeros) for more details.

consensus_plotprofile_per_group.description: Whether to plot all samples in a group together in the consensus peak profile plot. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/plotProfile.html#per-group) for more details.

input_cisrpm_in_plotprofile.description: Whether to include the input CISRPM signal in the gene or consensus peak profile plots.

save_macs_bdgcmp_intermeds.description: Save intermediate bedGraph/bigWig files generated by the MACS3 bdgcmp step.

edd_bin_size.description: Bin size (Kb) for EDD peak calling. Autoestimated if left blank. See [EDD documentation](https://github.com/CollasLab/edd) for more details.

edd_gap_penalty.description: Gap penalty for EDD peak calling. Autoestimated by EDD if left blank. See [EDD documentation](https://github.com/CollasLab/edd) for more details.

edd_num_trials.description: Number of Monte Carlo trials for EDD peak calling. See [EDD documentation](https://github.com/CollasLab/edd) for more details.

edd_fdr.description: FDR threshold for EDD peak calling. See [EDD documentation](https://github.com/CollasLab/edd) for more details.

save_genrich_pileup.description: Instruct Genrich to save pileup files.

epic2_binsize.description: Size of the windows to scan the genome in epic2. Bin size is the smallest possible island.

epic2_fdr.description: In epic2 peak calling, remove all islands with an FDR above this cutoff.

skip_encode_pipeline.description: Skip peak calling with the ENCODE ChIP-seq pipeline.

ctl_depth_ratio_threshold.description: For each sample, if the ratio of depth between input controls is higher than this, then a pooled input control will be used for all sample replicates.

use_best_multisummit_idr.description: Set the IDR value for a group of multi summit peaks (a group of peaks with the same chr/start/stop but different summits) to the best value across all of these peaks. This is a work around for peak callers that don't do a good job splitting scores across multi summit peaks (e.g. MACS). If set in conjunction with --plot two plots will be created - one with alternate summits and one without. Use this option with care. See the [IDR documentation](https://github.com/nboley/idr) for more details.

idr_soft_threshold.description: Report statistics for peaks with a global IDR below this value but return all peaks

idr_filtering_threshold.description: Filter peaks with an IDR above this value.

spp_npeak.description: Threshold on the number of peaks to call with SPP for the ENCODE-based processing.

encode_peak_max_score.description: Set peaks with a score above this value to this value.

xcor_exclusion_range_min.description: Minimum fragment length to exclude when calculating cross-correlation metrics for the ENCODE-based processing.

xcor_exclusion_range_max.description: Maximum fragment length to exclude when calculating cross-correlation metrics for the ENCODE-based processing. If not provided `max(params.read_length + 10, 100)` will be used.

seacr_peak_threshold.description: SEACR specifies returns the top n fraction (between 0 and 1) of peaks based on total signal within peaks. This is only used if there are no controls included with the samples and if `--use_control` is `false`

mace_kmer_size.description: Set the k-mer size for MACE peak calling. Kmer size [6,12] to correct nucleotide composition bias. kmerSize < 0.5*read_length. Larger KmerSize might make program slower. Set kmerSize = 0 to turn off nucleotide compsition bias correction. default=6. See the [MACE documentation](https://chipexo.sourceforge.net/) for more details.

mace_bin.description: Chromosome chunk size. Each chomosome will be cut into small chunks of this size. Decrease chunk size will save more RAM. default=100000 (bp). See the [MACE documentation](https://chipexo.sourceforge.net/) for more details.

mace_depth.description: Reference reads count (default = 10 million). Sequencing depth will be normailzed to this number, so that wig files are comparable between replicates. See the [MACE documentation](https://chipexo.sourceforge.net/) for more details.

mace_qcut.description: phred scaled mapping quality threshhold to determine “uniqueness” of alignments. default=30. See the [MACE documentation](https://chipexo.sourceforge.net/) for more details.

mace_norm_method.description: Method used to consolidate replicates and reduce noise. “EM” = Entropy weighted mean, “AM”=Arithmetic mean, “GM”=Geometric mean, “SNR”=Signal-to-noise ratio. See the [MACE documentation](https://chipexo.sourceforge.net/) for more details.

mace_pvalue.description: Pvalue cutoff for border detection and subsequent border pairing. default=0.05. See the [MACE documentation](https://chipexo.sourceforge.net/) for more details.

mace_max_dist.description: Maximum distance allowed for border pairing. default=100 (bp). See the [MACE documentation](https://chipexo.sourceforge.net/) for more details.

mace_fuzzy_size.description: Peaks (i.e. borders) located closely within this window will be merged. default=5 (bp). See the [MACE documentation](https://chipexo.sourceforge.net/) for more details.

mace_window_size.description: Background window size used to determine background signal level. default=100 (bp). See the [MACE documentation](https://chipexo.sourceforge.net/) for more details.

mace_signal_fold.description: Minimum coverage signal used to build model (i.e. estimate optimal peak pair size). default=2.0. See the [MACE documentation](https://chipexo.sourceforge.net/) for more details.

save_mace_intermeds.description: Whether to save the intermediate files from the MACE peak calling step. These include the MACE peak files in bedGraph format.

process_skipping_options.title: Process skipping options
process_skipping_options.description: Options to skip various steps within the workflow.

spikein_barcode_table.description: Path to a tab-delimited file containing the spike-in barcode targets, ids, and sequences. See the [sc_spikein_barcodes.tsv](https://github.com/grothlab/crepas/assets/barcodes/sc_spikein_barcodes.tsv) for an example. This is only useful for CUT&Tag or CUT&RUN experiments with SNAP-CUTANA™ Spike-ins (See https://support.epicypher.com/v1/docs/analyzing-snap-cutana-spike-in-controls-and-expected-results).

skip_spikein_barcode_extract.description: Whether to skip the extraction of spike-in barcodes from FASTQ files. This is useful for CUT&Tag or CUT&RUN experiments with SNAP-CUTANA™ Spike-ins (See https://support.epicypher.com/v1/docs/analyzing-snap-cutana-spike-in-controls-and-expected-results).

deseq2_vst.description: Use vst transformation instead of rlog with DESeq2.

genes_plotprofile_mode.description: Mode to compute the matrix for deepTools plotProfile. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/computeMatrix.html#named-arguments) for more details.

genes_plotprofile_ref_point.description: Reference point for deepTools plotProfile when `--genes_plotprofile_mode` is `reference_point`. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/computeMatrix.html#named-arguments) for more details.

genes_plotprofile_region_body_length.description: Region body length (in bp) for deepTools plotProfile when `--genes_plotprofile_mode` is `scale_regions`. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/computeMatrix.html#named-arguments) for more details.

genes_plotprofile_upstream.description: Upstream distance (in bp) from the reference point for deepTools plotProfile when `--genes_plotprofile_mode` is `reference_point`. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/computeMatrix.html#named-arguments) for more details.

genes_plotprofile_downstream.description: Downstream distance (in bp) from the reference point for deepTools plotProfile when `--genes_plotprofile_mode` is `reference_point`. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/computeMatrix.html#named-arguments) for more details.

genes_plotprofile_skip_zeros.description: Whether to skip regions with zero coverage in all samples when computing the matrix for deepTools plotProfile. This is determined BEFORE any applicable pseudocount is added. See the [deepTools documentation](https://deeptools.readthedocs.io/en/develop/content/tools/computeMatrix.html#named-arguments) for more details.

skip_spp_qc.description: Skip Phantompeakqualtools QC metrics and plots.

skip_deseq2_qc.description: Skip DESeq2 PCA and heatmap plotting.

skip_qc.description: Skip all QC steps except for MultiQC.

partition_and_rfd_analysis_options.title: SCAR-seq (partition) and OK-seq (RFD) analysis options
partition_and_rfd_analysis_options.description: Options to adjust SCAR-seq and OK-seq analysis criteria.

partition_fragment_size.description: For single-end SCAR-seq or OK-seq data, the fragment size (in bp) to extend reads when calculating coverage for partition/RFD analysis. For paired-end data, coverage of intervals is calculated from the left point of a read pair to the right point.

partition_window_size.description: Window/bin size (in bp) for dividing chromosomes when calculating coverage for partition/RFD analysis in SCAR-seq or OK-seq experiments. See [this reference](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aau0294#supplementary-materials) for more details.

partition_step_size.description: Step size (in bp) for sliding window when calculating coverage for partition/RFD analysis in SCAR-seq or OK-seq experiments. Default is the same as `--partition_window_size` to create fixed-size book-ended bins instead of sliding windows.

smooth_radius.description: Smoothing radius for partition/RFD signal smoothing. Smoothing is computed across consecutive book-ended bins, performing a uniform blur considering the neighboring bins on each side. See [this reference](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aau0294#supplementary-materials) for more details.

derivative_radius.description: Radius for [nonparametric derivative estimation](https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v055.i02) of RFD signal to detect sharp transitions between neighboring bins for initiation zone detection. See [this reference](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aau0294#supplementary-materials) for more details.

zero_crossing_radius.description: Radius for zero-crossing detection when defining replication initiation zones. See [this reference](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aau0294#supplementary-materials) for more details.

partition_rpm_cutoff.description: RPM (reads per million) cutoff for bins to be included in downstream partition analysis. Bins with normalized read-counts above this threshold will be included. See [this reference](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aau0294#supplementary-materials) for more details.

partition_plot_range.description: Distance (kb) up- and downstream of each initiation zone to plot.
partition_plot_range.help_text: Independent of `partition_iz_rm_overlap_range`: when `partition_plot_range` is the larger of the two, the plotted flanks can reach neighbouring initiation zones and a partition bin may then contribute to more than one profile.

partition_iz_rm_overlap_range.description: Distance (kb) around each initiation zone used to discard overlapping ones.
partition_iz_rm_overlap_range.help_text: Any initiation zone whose window of this radius overlaps another one is discarded before plotting. Set to 0 to skip the removal of overlapping initiation zones entirely and keep them all. Independent of `partition_plot_range`, so the plotted range can be widened without discarding more initiation zones.

partition_exclude_scaffolds.description: Whether to exclude scaffolds from partition plots. Scaffolds are defined as chromosomes whose name begins with 'chrUn' or contains a dot ('.').

partition_exclude_chromosomes.description: Comma-separated list of chromosomes to exclude from partition analysis. Typically sex chromosomes and mitochondrial chromosomes are excluded. See [this reference](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aau0294#supplementary-materials) for more details.

skip_partition_group_plot.description: Whether to skip the grouped partition plots, which combine all samples of the same antibody in a single plot. Per-sample partition plots are still generated.

save_partition_intermeds.description: Whether to save the intermediate files from the partition/RFD analysis step.

repliseq_analysis_options.title: Repli-seq analysis options
repliseq_analysis_options.description: Options to adjust Repli-seq replication-timing (RT) track analysis.

repliseq_bin_size.description: Bin size (in bp) used by deepTools `multiBamSummary` when counting reads per window for Repli-seq replication-timing (RT) tracks (e.g. 5000, 10000, 20000, 50000, 100000 for 5/10/20/50/100 kb resolution).

repliseq_replicate_method.description: How to combine early/late biological replicates when calculating the Repli-seq RT ratio. `paired` computes the ratio per matched early/late biological-replicate pair (matched by `biological_replicate`) and averages; `pooled` averages replicates within each phase first, then computes one ratio; `auto` chooses between the two via a correlation heuristic (see `--repliseq_pairing_threshold`).

repliseq_normalization.description: `cpm` only CPM-normalizes each Repli-seq replicate; `qn` additionally quantile-normalizes between replicates, on top of CPM.

repliseq_smooth.description: Smoothing strategy applied to the raw Repli-seq RT track.

repliseq_smooth_stage.description: Where smoothing enters the Repli-seq RT calculation. `replicate` smooths each replicate's normalized coverage track and then takes the early/late ratio; `ratio` takes the ratio first and smooths that. Only affects the smoothed track; the raw track is always the unsmoothed ratio.

repliseq_clamp_negative.description: Floor smoothed replicate coverage at zero before taking the Repli-seq early/late ratio. Coverage cannot be negative, but a loess fit can undershoot below it. Only applies with `--repliseq_smooth_stage replicate`.

repliseq_ratio_direction.description: Orientation of the Repli-seq log2 ratio. `early_over_late` makes high values early-replicating, which is the usual convention; `late_over_early` inverts it.

repliseq_loess_degree.description: Degree of the local polynomial fitted by loess when smoothing Repli-seq RT tracks.

repliseq_loess_family.description: Loess fitting family used when smoothing Repli-seq RT tracks. `symmetric` reweights to resist outliers, but is undefined on sequences where over half the residuals are exactly zero, in which case it falls back to `gaussian` for that sequence.

repliseq_loess_window.description: Width (in bp) of the loess smoothing window used when `--repliseq_smooth loess`. It is converted to a per-sequence span, so the same genomic scale is smoothed over on every sequence regardless of its length.

repliseq_loess_span.description: Loess span given directly, as a fraction of the bins on each sequence, used when `--repliseq_smooth loess`. Overrides `--repliseq_loess_window` when set. Because it is a fraction rather than a fixed width, a long chromosome is smoothed over a proportionally wider stretch of sequence than a short one.

repliseq_roll_k.description: Rolling-mean window size, in bins, used when `--repliseq_smooth roll`.

repliseq_corr_method.description: Correlation method used by the `--repliseq_replicate_method auto` heuristic.

repliseq_pairing_threshold.description: Under `--repliseq_replicate_method auto`, `paired` is chosen when (matched-replicate-pair average correlation - mismatched-replicate-pair average correlation) is at least this value; otherwise `pooled` is used.

repliseq_exclude_scaffolds.description: Exclude scaffolds and alternate sequences from the Repli-seq RT track. deepTools `multiBamSummary` bins every sequence in the BAM header, and these are short and usually barely covered, which makes their RT values meaningless. A sequence counts as one when its name begins with `chrUn`, ends with `_random`, `_alt` or `_fix`, or contains a dot. They are dropped before CPM normalization, so the normalization reflects primary-chromosome depth only.

repliseq_min_bin_reads.description: Fewest reads a bin needs across the early and late fractions combined to appear in the `.covered` copy of the Repli-seq ratio track. A bin with no reads in either fraction still gets a ratio of exactly log2(1/1) = 0, which is indistinguishable from a genuinely mid-replicating bin, so replication-timing domains are called on the covered copy while the unfiltered track keeps every bin.

skip_repliseq_domains.description: Skip calling domains of constant replication timing from the Repli-seq ratio track.

repliseq_domain_track.description: Which Repli-seq ratio track to segment into replication-timing domains. The default `both` segments the raw and the smoothed track. Set `smooth` or `raw` to segment only one.

repliseq_domain_classification.description: How to call each replication-timing domain. `binary` calls every domain early or late from the sign of its segment mean; `three_way` additionally calls domains whose mean sits within `--repliseq_domain_threshold` of zero as intermediate, i.e. replicating throughout S phase.

repliseq_domain_threshold.description: Half-width of the intermediate band around a segment mean of zero, in log2 ratio units. Only used with `--repliseq_domain_classification three_way`.

repliseq_domain_alpha.description: Significance level for accepting a change point in DNAcopy's circular binary segmentation of the Repli-seq ratio track.

repliseq_domain_min_width.description: Smallest number of bins a replication-timing domain may contain. DNAcopy's `segment()` accepts 2 to 5.

repliseq_domain_undo_sd.description: Merge adjacent replication-timing domains whose segment means differ by fewer than this many standard deviations. Zero or less turns the merging off.

repliseq_domain_smooth_outliers.description: Run DNAcopy's `smooth.CNA()` before segmenting, which pulls single-bin outliers towards their neighbours so that one noisy bin does not become its own domain.

repliseq_domain_seed.description: Random seed for replication-timing domain calling. DNAcopy locates change points with a permutation test, so without a fixed seed the same track segments slightly differently on every run.

skip_repliseq_gene_classification.description: Skip classifying genes by the S-phase fraction with the highest read density over their gene body.

repliseq_min_gene_reads.description: Fewest reads a gene needs summed over every S-phase fraction before it is classified. Genes below it are reported as `unclassified`, because with only a handful of reads the fraction with the highest density is decided by sampling noise.

repliseq_gene_min_margin.description: Fewest CPM by which the winning S-phase fraction must exceed the runner-up for a gene to be classified. Zero accepts any winner.

repliseq_skip_gene_plots.description: Skip the diagnostic plots of the Repli-seq gene classification. The classification table and BEDs are still written.

repliseq_skip_domain_plots.description: Skip the diagnostic plots of the Repli-seq replication-timing domains. The domain BEDs and QC are still written.

save_repliseq_intermeds.description: Whether to save the intermediate files from the Repli-seq RT-track analysis step (raw counts tables and raw, unsmoothed bedGraph tracks).

hr_repliseq_analysis_options.title: High-resolution Repli-seq analysis options
hr_repliseq_analysis_options.description: Options to adjust high-resolution (16-fraction) Repli-seq analysis.

hr_repliseq_bin_size.description: Bin size (in bp) used by deepTools `multiBamSummary` when counting reads per window for high-resolution Repli-seq. 50 kb is the usual resolution: a 30 min BrdU pulse at a fork speed of 1.8 kb/min labels at least 50 kb per fork.

hr_repliseq_normalization.description: How each S phase fraction is normalized before the Repli-seq array is built. `g1_filter` drops the bins a `G1` whole-genome control does not cover, the mappability correction, and keeps the fractions as reads per million. `g1_ratio` additionally replaces each fraction with log2 of its ratio to the control, floored at zero: a stricter correction, but because every fraction and the control share the same mean the floor zeroes about half of each fraction, and on H1 it collapses the initiation-zone calls from ~2950 to 9, so it should not be used to call features. `rpm` corrects for sequencing depth only. `auto` uses `g1_filter` when a `G1` fraction is present in the samplesheet and `rpm` otherwise.

hr_repliseq_g1_label.description: Value of the `rt_fraction` samplesheet column that marks the G1 whole-genome-sequencing control.

hr_repliseq_g1_min_rpm.description: Bins whose G1 control coverage is at or below this many reads per million are dropped, since their ratio to the control is undefined.

hr_repliseq_exclude_chromosomes.description: Comma-separated sequences to drop before building the array, matched by name. The default removes the sex chromosomes, whose copy number differs from the autosomes, and the mitochondrial genome, which does not replicate on the nuclear schedule. Set to an empty string to keep every sequence.

hr_repliseq_chromosomes.description: Comma-separated list of sequences to restrict the array to (e.g. `chr1,chr2,chr3`), which also sets the order of the output. Leave unset to use every sequence that survives the scaffold and sex-chromosome filtering.

hr_repliseq_birch_threshold.description: BIRCH clustering threshold used to group bins into replication features. Lower values split the array into more, smaller clusters.

hr_repliseq_birch_n_clusters.description: Number of BIRCH clusters to reduce the subclusters to. Leave unset to keep the subclusters themselves.

hr_repliseq_termination_max_size.description: Valleys in the replication-timing profile up to this size (in bp) are called termination sites; larger ones are called late constant-timing regions.

hr_repliseq_partition_priority.description: Order in which overlapping feature calls are resolved into the partition, in which every analysed bin belongs to exactly one feature. Later entries win, so the last one listed takes precedence.

hr_repliseq_s_phase_hours.description: Assumed length of S phase in hours. A timing transition region is traversed by a single fork, so its length divided by the stretch of S phase it spans gives that fork's speed; this sets how long that stretch is in minutes. The method's paper assumes 10 h, the longest of the five cell lines it profiles, and reports a median of 1.7-2.0 kb/min.

hr_repliseq_plot_chromosomes.description: Comma-separated list of chromosomes to draw a Repli-seq heatmap page for. Leave unset to draw every chromosome in the array.

hr_repliseq_mqc_chromosome.description: Chromosome whose Repli-seq heatmap is shown in the MultiQC report. Defaults to the first one drawn.

hr_repliseq_example_pages.description: How many pages of example features to add to the plots PDF. Each page draws one randomly chosen instance of every feature shape: the cluster-centroid rank profile with the feature's bins picked out, over the heatmap of the same bins. Set to 0 to leave them out.

hr_repliseq_example_flank_bins.description: How many bins to show either side of an example feature. Smaller zooms in on the shape itself, larger gives it more surrounding context.

hr_repliseq_example_seed.description: Seed for choosing which feature instances the example pages show, so that a rerun draws the same ones.

skip_hr_repliseq_plots.description: Skip the high-resolution Repli-seq heatmaps and feature summary plots.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

fingerprint_bins.description: Number of genomic bins to use when calculating deepTools fingerprint plot.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

crepas_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of grothlab/crepas-specific test dataset files.

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.
